outcomes.title: A shared foundation for 130 connectors
outcomes.summary: Replaced repeated authentication, pagination, retry, and resume logic with a shared REST framework, and changed authoring guidance to prevent the duplication returning.
outcomes.benefit: Framework fixes can now reach the migrated connectors through one implementation. The migration preserves connector-specific behavior and adds shared host-pinning and secret-redaction protections.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Broad, demonstrated adoption across approximately 130 connectors, with framework regression tests and a reported full source-suite run. The follow-up migration establishes adoption beyond a proposed abstraction.

metrics.label: connectors migrated
metrics.context: The merged migration enumerates approximately 130 source connectors adopting common/rest_source; this is adoption breadth, not a PR count.

outcomes.followUp: Extend the same test-gated migration to remaining bespoke connectors, prioritizing duplicated retry and authentication paths.
limitations: Adoption is demonstrated in repository code; production maintenance savings were not measured.

outcomes.title: A 20-minute test loop reduced to 1.6
outcomes.summary: Removed real retry sleeps and repeated parser, subprocess, and fixture costs from the warehouse backend test suite while preserving the reported test outcomes.
outcomes.benefit: Engineers working on warehouse sources get substantially faster feedback from the service-free test suite without removing assertions.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A substantial, repeatable development workflow improvement supported by before/after timing and implementation changes. Limited to the measured local, service-free workload.

metrics.label: local suite time
metrics.context: Author-reported single-process service-free suite; unchanged pass/skip/error outcomes. Environment-dependent errors remained.

metrics.label: faster feedback
metrics.context: Approximate speedup reported for the same service-free test workload, not all CI.

outcomes.followUp: Measure the same changes on CI hardware before estimating team-wide waiting time saved.
limitations: Local measurements; 66 environment-dependent errors remained unchanged. No claim of a 12× reduction in total CI time.

outcomes.title: Recovering failed warehouse imports safely
outcomes.summary: Added recovery for corrupt Delta logs, bounded memory-related repartitioning, and a path to coarsen tables that had been split too aggressively.
outcomes.benefit: Warehouse imports can recover without repeatedly worsening fragmentation. Review-driven changes also avoid redundant maintenance and protect the salvage path with a regression test.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Substantial subsystem reliability work with targeted recovery tests and reported end-to-end partition-coarsening validation. Related fixes are grouped so repair work does not earn separate volume credit.

metrics.label: row identities in E2E
metrics.context: The coarsening test compares full row-ID lists across the rewrite rather than counts alone.

extraPeople.rationale: Implemented the coarsening repair and materially reviewed the original recovery work, including the missing salvage test and duplicate-vacuum path.

outcomes.followUp: Track genuine OOMs separately from deploy-related heartbeat loss, then verify recovery and coarsening outcomes after rollout.
limitations: No measured fleet-wide incident reduction. Disk spilling is disabled by default and needs infrastructure configuration; coarsening is feature gated.

outcomes.title: Reuse parent data instead of re-fetching it
outcomes.summary: Reused a completed warehouse snapshot for fan-out endpoints instead of repeatedly fetching the parent list from the vendor API.
outcomes.benefit: Reduces redundant vendor requests while preserving a consistent parent snapshot. A Sentry issue-tag-values comparison returned the same 77 rows with a shorter run.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Measured improvement for a concrete end-to-end workload, backed by matching results and regression tests. The result is not extrapolated to the entire source fleet.

metrics.label: Sentry test sync
metrics.context: Author-reported devbox comparison for issue_tag_values; 77 rows through either parent source, with the gate forced on locally.

extraPeople.rationale: Prompted completed-snapshot pinning and removal of silently enabling billable parent syncs; the author confirmed both design changes.

outcomes.followUp: Use the added drift counters to expand rollout only where warehouse parent snapshots stay sufficiently fresh.
limitations: Feature gated. One real Sentry source was tested; timings for the two smaller child tables were explicitly described as noise.

outcomes.title: Version pins that keep source upgrades deliberate
outcomes.summary: Added explicit API-version declarations and per-source-instance pins, seeding existing versions and introducing a generic deprecation surface.
outcomes.benefit: Source maintainers can introduce a vendor API version without silently changing existing customer configurations. Stripe demonstrates runtime dispatch through the shared contract.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A shared maintenance capability adopted across source declarations, with actual runtime dispatch in Stripe. Breadth of declarations does not imply all vendors have multi-version runtime support.

metrics.label: released sources seeded
metrics.context: The PR documents existing version declarations seeded for 217 released sources; the versioning machinery leaves existing behavior unchanged.

outcomes.followUp: Prioritize the next vendor sunset and validate an explicit customer migration using the version-pin runbook.
limitations: Most sources retain their current hardcoded version until a later dispatch implementation.

outcomes.title: A shorter path to a fresh database
outcomes.summary: Squashed historical Django migrations to reduce fresh-database setup, then repaired schema-restore, duplicate-index, and partial-upgrade regressions.
outcomes.benefit: Fresh CI and development databases apply a shorter migration chain. The complete story includes the rollout repair work and the upgrade paths the first version missed.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Substantial shared workflow improvement, conservatively rated 3 because the initial rollout caused documented CI and upgrade regressions. Follow-up repairs are grouped into the original outcome.

metrics.label: fresh default database
metrics.context: The original PR reports approximately 20 minutes before and a final local fresh default-database run of about 5.5 minutes.

outcomes.followUp: Make partially migrated databases and restored schema dumps mandatory cases for the next migration squash.
limitations: The first rollout broke E2E restores and partial upgrades and created a duplicate index. Linked follow-ups repair those paths; net team-hours saved is unknown.

outcomes.title: Light worktrees with no second toolchain install
outcomes.summary: Let matching-lockfile worktrees borrow the main clone's Python and Node toolchain, preserving local-install precedence and refusing mismatched dependencies.
outcomes.benefit: Small edit-and-commit tasks avoid duplicated environments, and Python pre-commit checks work in a bare linked worktree.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A substantial development setup improvement with a documented end-to-end bare-shell test and explicit lockfile/mutation guards.

metrics.label: edit-and-commit worktree
metrics.context: Author-reported footprint for a light worktree versus the full setup; app-running worktrees still need the heavy setup.

outcomes.followUp: Make the lightweight path easy to discover and check whether engineers still create full environments for small changes.
limitations: Measured for edit-and-commit worktrees; no team-wide adoption or time-saved measurement.

outcomes.title: App previews available without a manual label
outcomes.summary: Enabled automatic hibernating app previews for eligible frontend PRs, with opt-out, draft handling, and teardown paths.
outcomes.benefit: Creates a direct route for reviewers to inspect the application behavior of a frontend change.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A bounded implemented workflow capability. The source says real label-driven dogfooding remained to be done, so estimated adoption and compute savings are not treated as outcomes.
outcomes.followUp: Check whether reviewers use the previews and whether preview readiness becomes part of the review workflow.
limitations: No verified post-merge adoption. Estimated VM hours in the PR are forecasts, not measured savings.

outcomes.title: Faster transformations on production ingestion
outcomes.summary: Reduced interpreter allocation and dispatch costs in the Rust HogVM. Production old/new pods were compared on the same EU ingestion traffic.
outcomes.benefit: The shared transformation runtime executes each event with lower latency. The evidence also captures a separate cohort call-site regression and its follow-up repair.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Broad shared-runtime benefit supported by a production before/after table with unchanged reported error rate and parity tests. Affected cohort consumers required an additional fix, disclosed here.

metrics.label: reported p90 execution
metrics.context: Author-reported same-window EU main analytics ingestion comparison, all transformations mixed. Source dashboards are private; the public PR records the figures.

metrics.label: reported p50 latency
metrics.context: 0.34 ms to 0.23 ms in the same reported production comparison.

extraPeople.rationale: Identified missing token-decode and chunk-switch coverage; the author added the requested regression tests before merge.

outcomes.followUp: Audit other HogVM consumers for decode-on-every-evaluation behavior before widening runtime changes.
limitations: Production figures are author-reported, not independently reproduced. A cohort consumer paid repeated decode costs; PR #95610 addresses that separately.

outcomes.title: Decode cohort conditions once, not per event
outcomes.summary: Moved condition bytecode decoding into catalog construction so repeated cohort evaluations reuse a decoded program.
outcomes.benefit: Avoids repeatedly allocating thousands of string literals for large membership conditions, addressing a concrete integration cost of the new HogVM representation.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Substantial hot-path improvement shown for an explicitly scoped microbenchmark, with parity and malformed-program handling changes. No throughput extrapolation.

metrics.label: 8,000-string IN evaluation
metrics.context: One reported scratch microbenchmark run on a dev machine; smaller four-condition timing was near run-to-run noise.

outcomes.followUp: Measure the catalog-build cost and production evaluation distribution before estimating throughput gains.
limitations: Single-machine microbenchmark. Malformed programs now drop at catalog construction; rollout monitoring is required.

outcomes.title: Faster account lists with scoped database reads
outcomes.summary: Pushed tenant filtering into federated Postgres reads and combined compatible aggregating joins for Customer Analytics account queries.
outcomes.benefit: Account lists with custom properties avoid scanning unrelated rows. The benchmark verifies identical result hashes while making the latency and memory trade-off explicit.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A substantial measured workflow improvement with repeated HTTP benchmarks and correctness checks, conservatively scoped to the tested account configurations.

metrics.label: 10k accounts + 5 properties
metrics.context: Median of 10 real HTTP requests per scenario, with byte-identical result hashes; not a fleet-wide latency measurement.

outcomes.followUp: Validate the rollout on large accounts while monitoring memory before widening the feature flag.
limitations: At 100k accounts the relative improvement shrinks. The largest tested scenario increased peak memory from 132 MB to about 315 MB.

outcomes.title: A supported bridge from accounts to Slack channels
outcomes.summary: Extracted a conversations facade that Customer Analytics could use without importing another product's internals. The announcement API and send workflow then adopted that contract.
outcomes.benefit: The delivered stack gives account managers a compose, preview, and delivery flow while keeping product boundaries explicit.
outcomes.significanceRationale: An explicit cross-engineer dependency chain, from facade to API to asynchronous delivery to UI. The whole stack is one outcome rather than five PRs of credit.

metrics.label: documented dependency chain
metrics.context: The stacked PR descriptions explicitly identify the dependency sequence, and the API imports the conversations facade.

extraPeople.rationale: Built the model, API, send task, and UI that consume the conversations facade; the stack explicitly links its dependencies.

outcomes.followUp: Reuse the facade contract for other cross-product channel integrations, while validating actual announcement adoption.
limitations: The announcement feature is flag gated; customer usage and rollout coverage are not established by the public PRs.

outcomes.title: Previewable rules for which accounts stay visible
outcomes.summary: Added versioned account rules, a shared preview/execution compiler, controlled application, and recorded run history.
outcomes.benefit: Provides admins a tested way to replace stale one-off account updates with repeatable, inspectable rules.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A concrete implemented capability with backend, frontend, and devbox validation. Rated bounded because the source explicitly starts rollout at 0%.
outcomes.followUp: Use a small rollout to validate that preview results match admin expectations before enabling rules broadly.
limitations: The feature flag starts at 0%; customer benefit has not been established.

outcomes.title: Reusable widgets with controlled shared updates
outcomes.summary: Added a searchable widget catalog, reviewed version publishing, pinned placements, and draft isolation for widgets reused across notebooks.
outcomes.benefit: Notebook authors can reuse a capability and propagate a reviewed improvement without copying notebook-local code or unexpectedly replacing pinned versions.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Substantial product workflow spanning discovery, publication, versioning, and consumption, supported by functional tests and recorded browser checks. Usage is not measured.

extraPeople.rationale: Identified source-data access, client bytecode, and draft/live-build isolation risks; the final implementation and tests address these paths.

outcomes.followUp: Validate the catalog with a small set of reusable internal widgets and review access checks at every reuse boundary.
limitations: No public measurement of active users or saved authoring time. The review history is part of the outcome, not an approval-count signal.

outcomes.title: One appropriate test layer for each chart behavior
outcomes.summary: Separated chart-only rendering from full-page testing and removed duplicate full-mount checks only after identifying surviving regression coverage.
outcomes.benefit: Product Analytics retains its chart behavior checks with less expensive, clearer test ownership.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A subsystem-level simplification with named surviving coverage and before/after runtime, not credit for deleted lines or tests.

metrics.label: local insight suite
metrics.context: Reported local wall time after test-harness and coverage consolidation; unrelated to overall CI duration.

outcomes.followUp: Apply the same coverage-mapping approach to other slow suites before deleting tests or adding more workers.
limitations: Local test timing; the regression-coverage mapping is the justification for simplification.

outcomes.title: Retiring the unused insight conversion path
outcomes.summary: Removed the legacy filters-to-query converter after checking that no production caller remained, while preserving the live series helpers and their tests.
outcomes.benefit: Insight maintainers have one fewer obsolete transformation path to reason about, and module names match the functions callers actually use.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A subsystem cleanup justified by caller analysis, preserved live exports, and test coverage across consumers. File or line deletion counts do not affect significance.
outcomes.followUp: Continue the legacy-insight removal only after verifying each remaining consumer and its surviving regression tests.
limitations: Internal maintenance benefit; no measured user-performance or team-time gain.

outcomes.title: One executable plan for checking whether a fix helped
outcomes.summary: Unified expected-impact goals and executable follow-up checks, with full post-resolution query windows, atomic replacement, and independent approval.
outcomes.benefit: A report's displayed measurement plan and its scheduled checks use the same records, reducing false claims based on pre-fix data or failed persistence.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A substantial end-to-end product workflow with timing, permissions, concurrency, and rollback tests. Three dependent layers are grouped as one outcome.
outcomes.followUp: Audit a sample of resolved reports to verify that verdicts use a full post-fix window and that inconclusive results remain understandable.
limitations: Rollout is staged and metric suggestions remain gated. No observed customer adoption or fix-success rate is claimed.

outcomes.title: Parallel tests without wiping shared state
outcomes.summary: Moved eligible serial suites to isolated team fixtures and the parallel lane, preserving genuinely timing-sensitive cases in serial execution.
outcomes.benefit: Node developers wait less for the serial lane while avoiding cross-test interference in shared Postgres, Kafka, and Redis services.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A substantial test-workflow improvement with full-lane comparisons and explicit rejected migrations. The unmerged ingestion follow-up is not credited.

metrics.label: local serial lane
metrics.context: Reported same-machine lane comparison; parallel lane changed from 79 to 81 seconds. CI hardware was not checked.

outcomes.followUp: Validate on CI hardware, then address the remaining worker-isolation constraints before moving more suites.
limitations: Local timings. Follow-up PR #89866 was not merged at the snapshot and is excluded from scoring.

outcomes.title: A busy scrubber no longer takes its consumer down
outcomes.summary: Separated unavailable-sidecar failures from fatal consumer failures and handled batch deadlines and revoked-partition offset errors without terminating the consumer.
outcomes.benefit: Breaks a failure mechanism where a busy image scrubber causes consumer exits and rebalances that spread saturation to other pods.
outcomes.significanceRationale: A concrete production failure mechanism documented with logs and addressed with targeted error-path tests. Rated 3 because a post-deploy recovery measurement is not available.
outcomes.followUp: Check consumer restart rates alongside dropped-image counts to verify availability improved without hiding lost scrubbing work.
limitations: The source records the pre-fix crash loop; it does not establish a measured post-rollout incident reduction.

outcomes.title: One shared database build across query runners
outcomes.summary: Connected eight query runners to the existing shared per-run HogQL database, including SQL insights, events, people, groups, and session views.
outcomes.benefit: The shared foundation reaches consumers that previously bypassed it. Events and actor queries avoid constructing the same database twice in a run.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Demonstrated adoption of a shared capability across multiple query surfaces, with tests asserting one database construction and preserved SQL semantics.

metrics.label: builds in affected queries
metrics.context: Events and validating actors queries are documented examples; seven parameterized runner tests check the shared path.

outcomes.followUp: Use the new build-trigger counter to find remaining callers that still construct the database redundantly.
limitations: No measured fleet-wide latency reduction. Direct-connection queries intentionally keep their connection-scoped build.

outcomes.title: One uv setup contract across CI workflows
outcomes.summary: Adopted a shared uv setup action across compatible GitHub and Depot steps, retaining explicit exceptions for workflows checking out older revisions.
outcomes.benefit: Routine uv upgrades no longer require duplicating the same version and cache wiring across most CI steps.
outcomes.significanceRationale: Shared maintenance simplification backed by adoption and a structural comparison preserving workflow controls. No runtime speedup is claimed.

metrics.label: setup steps consolidated
metrics.context: PR-reported setup-step adoption; 15 retain direct pins because their checkout may lack the composite action.

outcomes.followUp: Keep exceptions tied to checkout contracts so future migrations do not break workflows running older revisions.
limitations: A maintainability result, not a measurement of CI minutes saved.

outcomes.title: A reusable first-run experience inside each product
outcomes.summary: Introduced a shared product empty-state contract and adopted it in MCP Analytics, using real data-existence signals instead of dismissal flags.
outcomes.benefit: A first-time user can see product-specific setup in context, and the product becomes available when real data arrives.
outcomes.significanceRationale: An implemented user workflow with one reference adoption. Broader adoption is not assumed from the presence of a reusable component.
outcomes.followUp: Evaluate the MCP Analytics setup flow before migrating other products to the shared gate.
limitations: One reference adoption; no measured activation-rate improvement.
